evals.name: pure linear chain plans one ticket per wave, all serial
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/linear-demo/ — the ticket set is 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: 01), 03 (Blocked by: 02). The parent spec.md names a single eval-harness test seam for the whole feature, and each ticket has one acceptance criterion. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Wave 0 = {01}, wave 1 = {02}, wave 2 = {03} — each ticket is blocked only by the previous one, so no two tickets share a wave. The Plan's wave table shows, per ticket, its estimated touch-set, a serial disposition with the reason (blocked by the prior ticket), no overlap flag, the eval-harness test seam, and the retry budgets MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3 and MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES = 3. There is a wave table and no model column. Stage 0 stops for explicit approval without writing to any source file.
expectations: Assigns waves 0, 1, 2 to 01, 02, 03 respectively, derived from the Blocked by edges
Marks every ticket serial because each depends on the previous ticket, with no overlap flag
Shows wave, touch-set, disposition, test seam, and retry budgets per ticket in the wave table, with no model column
Pauses for explicit approval and creates or modifies no file outside .scratch/linear-demo/

evals.name: independent tickets are still planned to run serially
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/independent-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: None), 03 (Blocked by: 01, 02). Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: 01 and 02 have no edge between them but the run still works them one after another in ascending ticket-number order, then 03. The Plan does not propose parallel execution; execution is serial because one local model instance serializes inference regardless (parallelism is a non-goal, not a deferred follow-up).
expectations: Orders the run 01, 02, 03 and works one ticket at a time
Does not dispatch 01 and 02 concurrently and proposes no wave
States that parallelism is a non-goal for a single local model
Pauses for approval before any source file changes

evals.name: cyclic ticket set is rejected up front
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/cyclic-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: 03), 02 (Blocked by: 01), 03 (Blocked by: 02). Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: The dependency graph has a cycle 01 -> 03 -> 02 -> 01. The run halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_CYCLIC), naming the tickets in the cycle, before computing the dependency order or writing anything.
expectations: Detects the cycle and halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_CYCLIC)
Names the specific tickets forming the cycle
Halts before any other planning work and before touching any file
Dispatches no worker

evals.name: missing blocker is rejected up front
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/missing-blocker-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: 07). Ticket 07 does not exist. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Ticket 02 names a non-existent blocker 07. The run halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_MISSING_BLOCKER), naming ticket 02 and the dangling reference 07, before any other work.
expectations: Detects the unresolvable blocker and halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_MISSING_BLOCKER)
Names ticket 02 and the dangling reference to 07
Halts before computing the dependency order or touching any file

evals.name: numbering inconsistent with topological order is rejected
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/numbering-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: 02), 02 (Blocked by: None). Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Ticket 01 is blocked by the higher-numbered ticket 02, so the numbering is not consistent with a topological order. The run halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_NUMBERING) naming 01 and 02.
expectations: Detects the numbering inconsistency and halts with BLOCKED (TICKET_SET_NUMBERING)
Names both ticket 01 and ticket 02
Halts before touching any file

evals.name: wave computation from independent branches assigns each ticket its wave
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/wavebranch-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: None), 03 (Blocked by: 01), 04 (Blocked by: 02). 01/03 and 02/04 are two independent dependency branches. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: Wave 0 = {01, 02} — both have an empty Blocked by set. Wave 1 = {03, 04} — 03's only blocker (01) and 04's only blocker (02) each landed in wave 0. The wave table shows each ticket's wave, its estimated touch-set, a serial/parallel proposal with overlap flags, its test seam, and the retry budgets — no model column. Stops for explicit approval without writing to any source file.
expectations: Assigns wave 0 to 01 and 02, since both have an empty Blocked by set
Assigns wave 1 to 03 and 04, since each one's only blocker landed in the previous wave
Treats 01/02 as independent candidates within wave 0 and 03/04 as independent candidates within wave 1
Shows wave, touch-set, disposition+overlap flags, test seam, and retry budgets per ticket, with no model column
Pauses for explicit approval and creates or modifies no file outside .scratch/wavebranch-demo/

evals.name: a same-wave overlapping touch-set pair is flagged likely-overlapping
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/overlap-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (Blocked by: None), 02 (Blocked by: None). Both are estimated to modify src/reports/list.ts. Present the Plan.
evals.expected_output: 01 and 02 both land in wave 0 with no Blocked by edge between them. The Plan flags {01, 02} 'likely-overlapping — consider serializing' because their estimated touch-sets intersect on src/reports/list.ts, with the default suggestion to serialize. The user decides at Plan approval whether to serialize or run them in parallel anyway — the integration gate, not this heuristic, is the correctness guarantee.
expectations: Places 01 and 02 together in wave 0 as independent tickets
Raises the likely-overlapping — consider serializing flag on the 01/02 pair with the touch-set intersection as the reason
States serialize as the default suggestion but leaves the choice to the user at Plan approval
Notes the integration gate, not the touch-set heuristic, is the correctness guarantee

evals.name: no source is mutated before Plan approval
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/readonly-demo/ — a valid three-ticket set. Present the Plan, then stop.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator produces the Plan and pauses. No file outside .scratch/readonly-demo/ is created or modified: no integration branch, no worktree, no worker dispatch, no opencode.json.
expectations: Emits the Plan and pauses for explicit approval
Creates or modifies no file outside .scratch/readonly-demo/
Creates no integration branch, no worktree, and dispatches no worker

evals.name: no argument resolves to the most recently modified issues directory
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement — no argument. The most recently modified .scratch/*/issues/ directory is .scratch/subtitle-preferences/issues/.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator selects .scratch/subtitle-preferences/issues/, names it back to the user, and waits for confirmation before parsing the tickets.
expectations: Selects the most recently modified .scratch/*/issues/ directory
Names the resolved directory back to the user
Waits for confirmation before parsing or planning

evals.name: an opencode failure inside the retry budget is retried locally, not escalated
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/retry-demo/ — the Plan is approved. The first opencode run for ticket 01 sub-step 1 emits an {"type":"error"} event and exits non-zero. This is the first opencode failure for this sub-step.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator treats it as an opencode failure (not a verification failure), re-dispatches a fresh opencode run for the same sub-step with a progress note naming the failure, and does not escalate — MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES = 3 has not been reached. It does not resume the session with -s.
expectations: Classifies the error event + non-zero exit as an opencode failure
Re-dispatches a fresh opencode session (not -s resume) with a progress note
Does not escalate to the subagent fallback while retries remain
Counts it against MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES, not MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS

evals.name: a worker that emits no first event is killed as an opencode failure
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/hang-demo/ — the Plan is approved. The opencode run for ticket 01 sub-step 1 has produced no step_start event and FIRST_EVENT_TIMEOUT has elapsed.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator kills the worker PID, records it as an opencode failure (a hung run produces nothing at all), and re-dispatches a fresh worker, counting one MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES attempt. STALL_INTERVAL and WORKER_TIMEOUT are the other two kill conditions.
expectations: Kills the worker on FIRST_EVENT_TIMEOUT with no step_start seen
Records an opencode failure and re-dispatches, counting a retry
Treats STALL_INTERVAL and WORKER_TIMEOUT as the other kill conditions

evals.name: a hung or slow smoke test stops the run before it starts
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/smoke-demo/ — the Plan is approved. The preflight smoke test opencode run produces no first event within FIRST_EVENT_TIMEOUT.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator does not begin the run. It stops with a message telling the user to free up or restart Ollama and opencode, having created the integration branch and gitignore entry but dispatched no ticket worker.
expectations: Runs the smoke test with nothing else using the local model before the first real dispatch
Stops the whole run on a slow/stuck/failed smoke test
Tells the user to free up or restart Ollama / opencode
Dispatches no ticket worker

evals.name: the sub-step worker prompt is self-contained and test-first
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/prompt-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Show the worker prompt the orchestrator writes for ticket 01 sub-step 2 of 3.
evals.expected_output: The prompt at .scratch/prompt-demo/prompts/01/2.md carries: the absolute worktree path; the ticket's What-to-build for orientation; this sub-step's one acceptance criterion verbatim; a progress note from sub-step 1 (files changed, test status); the named spec sections, ADRs, glossary, and test seam; the files in scope; the full red-green-refactor protocol inline; the constraints (touch only files in scope, commit on the worker branch, no push/PR, no package install, no repo scan, stop on a missing decision, treat /word as literal text); and the required structured return.
expectations: Includes the one sub-step criterion verbatim and the progress note
Carries the red-green-refactor protocol inline
Names spec sections rather than the whole spec, and lists the files in scope
Requires a structured return: red output, green output, files changed, test to criterion

evals.name: a one-criterion ticket runs end to end and lands as one commit
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/e2e-demo/ — a single ticket 01 (Blocked by: None) with one acceptance criterion. The Plan is approved. The opencode worker writes a failing test, makes it pass, and returns a well-formed red/green report.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator runs the one sub-step, passes the checkpoint check, runs the verification gate (reproduce red at the pre-ticket HEAD with only the test file, confirm coverage and non-vacuity, run green + typecheck), and squash-merges the worker branch onto opencode-implement/e2e-demo as one commit named for the ticket that also ticks its checkboxes. The worktree is removed.
expectations: Runs the checkpoint check after the sub-step and the full verification gate after the chain
Reproduces the red state itself at the pre-ticket integration HEAD
Squash-merges one commit per ticket in ticket-number order and ticks the checkboxes
Removes the worktree after the integrated suite is green

evals.name: a multi-criterion chain carries state by commit and progress note, never -s resume
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/chain-demo/ — ticket 01 has three acceptance criteria. The Plan is approved with a three-sub-step step plan.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator dispatches sub-step 1, has the worker commit on the worker branch, runs the checkpoint, writes a progress note (files changed, test status), then dispatches sub-step 2 as a fresh opencode session with that progress note — not opencode run -s. Same for sub-step 3. The verification gate runs once, after sub-step 3.
expectations: Commits each sub-step on the worker branch and writes a progress note between sub-steps
Dispatches each sub-step as a fresh opencode session, never -s resume
Runs the checkpoint check per sub-step and the verification gate once at the end

evals.name: a sub-step that overflows at runtime is re-split, not failed
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/resplit-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Ticket 01 sub-step 2's worker returns a truncated edit and a green run that does not actually cover the criterion; the checkpoint check fails with overflow symptoms.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator recognises the overflow, re-splits sub-step 2 along a natural line (by file or layer) into finer sub-steps, records the re-split in status.md, and runs the finer sub-steps. The re-split is not counted against MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS — the wrong size estimate is the plan's fault.
expectations: Detects the overflow from the checkpoint failure plus symptoms (truncated edit, uncovered criterion)
Re-splits sub-step 2 into finer sub-steps and records it in status.md
Does not count the re-split against MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS

evals.name: a fabricated / not-actually-red test fails verification
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/notred-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Ticket 01's worker returns a green report, but when the orchestrator applies only the new test file at the pre-ticket HEAD it passes without the implementation.
evals.expected_output: The verification gate's red reproduction fails: the test passes without the implementation, so it never measured a missing behaviour. This is a verification failure; the orchestrator re-dispatches the failing sub-step with that specific detail, up to MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3.
expectations: Runs the orchestrator's own red reproduction rather than trusting the worker's pasted output
Treats a test that passes without the implementation as a verification failure
Re-dispatches the failing sub-step with the specific failure, counting a MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS attempt

evals.name: a vacuous test and missing criterion coverage each fail verification
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/vacuous-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Ticket 01 has two criteria. The worker's return includes one test that is expect(true).toBe(true) and leaves the second criterion with no test.
evals.expected_output: The verification gate rejects the ticket on two counts: the vacuous assertion, and the acceptance criterion with no covering test. The orchestrator re-dispatches with both details, up to MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3.
expectations: Flags expect(true).toBe(true) as a vacuous test
Flags the acceptance criterion left uncovered by any new test
Re-dispatches the failing sub-step(s) rather than integrating

evals.name: a design-encoding merge conflict is surfaced, not resolved
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/conflict-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Integrating ticket 03's verified worker branch conflicts with ticket 02's commit over which module owns a shared validation contract.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator recognises the conflict encodes a design decision (module ownership of a shared contract), halts with BLOCKED (INTEGRATION_DESIGN_CONFLICT), and surfaces the decision to the user. It does not pick a side. Ticket 03 returns to Stage 0.
expectations: Distinguishes a design-encoding conflict from a mechanical one
Halts with BLOCKED (INTEGRATION_DESIGN_CONFLICT) and surfaces the decision
Does not resolve the conflict itself or write ticket implementation code

evals.name: three failed local verification attempts escalate to the subagent with no pause
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/escalate-demo/ — the Plan is approved, fallback is on (default). Ticket 01 fails the verification gate three times on the local model.
evals.expected_output: After the third failure the orchestrator discards ticket 01's partial worktree and worker branch, cuts a fresh worker branch from integration HEAD, and dispatches one native subagent (subagent_type = general-purpose, isolation: worktree) for the whole ticket — with no approval pause. The ticket's path becomes subagent-fallback and the escalation is recorded in status.md.
expectations: Escalates automatically after MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3 local verification failures, with no approval pause
Discards the partial local worktree and worker branch and starts the subagent from clean integration HEAD
Dispatches one native subagent for the whole ticket via the Agent tool, never fork
Records the escalation and its trigger in status.md and sets the path to subagent-fallback

evals.name: TICKET_TOO_LARGE_FOR_CONTEXT escalates directly with fallback on
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/toolarge-demo/ — fallback is on (default). Ticket 02 has a single acceptance criterion that cannot be split fine enough to fit the context budget even after re-splitting by file and layer.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator does not BLOCK. It escalates ticket 02 straight to the subagent fallback (TICKET_TOO_LARGE_FOR_CONTEXT trigger), running the whole ticket from clean integration HEAD and verifying with the same gate.
expectations: Recognises the criterion cannot be split under budget and triggers the fallback, not a BLOCK
Runs the subagent for the whole ticket and verifies with the orchestrator's gate

evals.name: --no-fallback turns the too-large trigger into a BLOCK
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement --no-fallback .scratch/strict-demo/ — same as toolarge-demo: ticket 02's one criterion cannot be split under the context budget.
evals.expected_output: With --no-fallback the orchestrator does not escalate. Ticket 02 becomes BLOCKED (TICKET_TOO_LARGE_FOR_CONTEXT). The run spends zero Claude tokens and no code leaves the machine.
expectations: Suppresses the subagent fallback entirely under --no-fallback / --strict-local
Produces BLOCKED (TICKET_TOO_LARGE_FOR_CONTEXT) instead of escalating
Spends no Claude tokens

evals.name: opencode failures past the retry budget escalate to the subagent
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/opencodefail-demo/ — fallback is on. Ticket 01 sub-step 1's opencode run fails (error event / timeout kill) four times: three retries then a fourth attempt.
evals.expected_output: MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES = 3 is exhausted, so the ticket escalates to the subagent fallback (opencode-failures-exhausted trigger), from clean integration HEAD. An opencode hiccup within the budget would have been retried locally instead.
expectations: Retries opencode failures up to MAX_OPENCODE_RETRIES = 3 locally
Escalates to the subagent fallback once that budget is exhausted
Does not escalate an opencode hiccup that is still within the retry budget

evals.name: the fallback subagent also failing its budget is the only BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED)
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/blocked-demo/ — fallback is on. Ticket 01 escalated to the subagent, which then fails the verification gate three times.
evals.expected_output: Only after the fallback subagent exhausts its own MAX_TICKET_ATTEMPTS = 3 does ticket 01 become BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED), with the failure output recorded and the worktree kept. The orchestrator never hand-codes the ticket.
expectations: Reaches BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED) only when the fallback subagent also fails its full budget
Keeps the worktree and records the failure output
Does not implement the ticket itself to rescue the run

evals.name: every escalation is disclosed in status.md and the handoff
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/disclose-demo/ — a five-ticket run where ticket 03 took the subagent fallback and the rest ran local.
evals.expected_output: status.md records ticket 03's path as subagent-fallback with its trigger and tokens.fallback. The completion handoff names ticket 03 explicitly: 'ticket 03: subagent fallback — Claude tokens spent, code left the machine', alongside the per-path token totals (local = cost 0).
expectations: Records the fallback path, trigger, and token usage per ticket in status.md
Names each fallback ticket in the handoff with its Claude token spend and the privacy note
Reports per-path token totals with local runs at cost 0

evals.name: a BLOCKED ticket halts only its dependency branch
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/partial-demo/ — ticket set: 01 (None), 02 (01), 03 (01), 04 (02). Ticket 02 becomes BLOCKED (TICKET_VERIFICATION_FAILED) after its fallback also fails. 01 and 03 are already integrated.
evals.expected_output: 01 and 03 stay integrated. 04 is not started because it is transitively blocked by 02. The run stops at the next frontier and the halt report names ticket 02 (with its reason), names 04 as not started, and reports that 03's branch is complete. The resume command is /opencode-implement continue partial-demo.
expectations: Keeps 01 and 03 integrated and stops 04 as transitively blocked by 02
Halts at the next frontier rather than the whole run
Names the blocked ticket, its reason, and the downstream tickets not started
Prints the /opencode-implement continue command

evals.name: status.md records the per-ticket fields and the integration ref
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement status subtitle-preferences — the run has 01 integrated (local), 02 in progress at sub-step 2 of 3 (local), 03 not started.
evals.expected_output: The read-only status report shows the ticket table in dependency order with each ticket's status, path, and blockers; 02's sub_step position; cumulative per-path token totals (local = cost 0); the integration branch ref opencode-implement/subtitle-preferences and its commit. It mutates nothing.
expectations: Shows status, path, and blockers per ticket and 02's sub-step position
Reports cumulative per-path token totals and the integration branch ref
Mutates no file

evals.name: continue discards a half-built ticket and re-dispatches it from clean
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement continue crash-demo — status.md records ticket 03 as 'verifying' when the session died; its worker branch opencode-implement/crash-demo/03 and worktree exist with commits. 01 and 02 are integrated and still verify.
evals.expected_output: Reality reconciliation confirms 01 and 02 still verify, then discards ticket 03's worker branch and worktree (a killed opencode worker can leave an odd git state) and re-dispatches ticket 03 from clean integration HEAD. It re-presents the Plan and resumes from ticket 03.
expectations: Re-verifies the committed tickets 01 and 02 before trusting status.md
Discards the half-built worker branch and worktree for ticket 03
Re-dispatches ticket 03 from clean integration HEAD and re-presents the Plan

evals.name: continue rewinds the integration branch when a committed ticket no longer verifies
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement continue drift-demo — status.md records 01, 02, 03 integrated. On re-verification ticket 02's tests now fail because the user hand-edited a file.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator resets the integration branch to ticket 01's commit (the last still-verifying commit), discards the worktrees for 02 and 03, lists the discarded commits (02 and 03) at the top of the report, and re-dispatches from ticket 02. The Plan is re-presented against this reconciled reality.
expectations: Detects that committed ticket 02 no longer verifies
Resets the integration branch to the last still-verifying commit (01)
Lists the discarded commits at the top of the report
Re-dispatches from ticket 02

evals.name: a dirty target tree at preflight stops the run
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/dirty-demo/ — the Plan is approved but the target repository has uncommitted changes.
evals.expected_output: Preflight halts the run and asks the user to deal with the uncommitted changes. It does not stash anything, does not create the integration branch, and dispatches no worker.
expectations: Detects the dirty tree at preflight and stops
Does not stash or auto-commit the user's changes
Creates no integration branch and dispatches no worker

evals.name: a worker that needs a new dependency stops and is replanned
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/dep-demo/ — the Plan is approved. Ticket 01 sub-step 1's worker reports that the criterion needs a new third-party package that is not installed.
evals.expected_output: The worker stops and reports the missing dependency rather than running a package install. The orchestrator returns ticket 01 to Stage 0 planning as a dependency decision; the shared lockfile is untouched.
expectations: The worker stops and reports rather than running npm/pip/cargo install
The orchestrator treats a new dependency as a planning decision and replans
The shared lockfile is not mutated

evals.name: the completion handoff names the branch and the review commands and never pushes
evals.prompt: /opencode-implement .scratch/handoff-demo/ — all four tickets integrated, the last suite green, all local.
evals.expected_output: The handoff prints: all 4 tickets integrated onto opencode-implement/handoff-demo, one commit per ticket in dependency order; per-path token usage (local, cost 0); and the exact commands /code-review since <merge-base with main> then /scrutinize to run in a fresh context. It performs no review, no git push, and opens no PR.
expectations: Names the integration branch and confirms one commit per ticket
Prints /code-review since <merge-base> and /scrutinize as the next step
Runs no review and does not push or open a PR
